title: Stable fractions for each depth label permit either sign of the ComCat shallow-share change between 2000-2012 and 2013-2025
abstract: We tested how the group used for a stable depth assumption affects a shallow-share comparison in 12,848 global ComCat events with preferred M >= 5.5. We reused a published snapshot and compared 2000-2012 with 2013-2025 at depth <= 15 km. Treating exact 10, 33 and 35 km records as one group with a stable unknown shallow fraction gives a change of +1.43 to +7.62 percentage points. Stable fractions for each label instead permit -3.63 to +12.68 points. The labels change in composition. A continuous drift of 4.31 points removes the positive lower bound in the pooled model; a finite witness uses 86 late flagged records. All bounds assume correct classifications outside the three labels. These are deterministic sensitivity results, not measured true depth changes or confidence intervals. Source errors, mixed origins and magnitudes, selected periods and untested stability assumptions limit inference. The package includes code, aggregate counts, bound witnesses, a drift curve, provenance and a separate count audit. External event records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Exact depth labels change in composition. Stable pooled and label-specific shallow fractions give different bounds. Solid curves are lower bounds; dashed curves are upper bounds. Bounds assume correct nonflagged classifications.

citations.reason: We reuse the source snapshot, periods, flags and cutoff; we add stability and drift sensitivity models. This is the same data, not independent confirmation.
Prior assigned-depth audit informs the uncertainty model.
Prior boundary sensitivity audit provides context; its data are not reused.
